features.name: Palampet / Ramappa
features.fact: on Aug 31 the Centre/ASI notified the Kakatiya-era Gollala Gudi — a trikutalaya (three-shrine) temple beside Ramappa — as a Monument of National Importance under the AMASR Act, 1958.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Gollala Gudi, Palampet — Mulugu district, Telangana. Palampet lies in northeastern Telangana on the Deccan plateau, in the Godavari basin north-east of Warangal (Mulugu was carved out of Warangal in 2019); it already hosts the Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2021.

features.name: Sriharikota
features.fact: ISRO flew GSLV-F17 with EOS-05 at 02:55 IST on Sep 4, placing the 2,367-kg satellite — the GSLV's heaviest payload yet — into a sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Sriharikota & the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) — Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh. A barrier island on the Bay of Bengal that separates Pulicat Lake (India's second-largest brackish lagoon, shared with Tamil Nadu) from the sea, roughly 80 km north of Chennai; the spindle-shaped island gives an eastward over-sea launch corridor and sits close to the equator.

features.name: Prayagraj / Sangam
features.fact: around Sep 1 both rivers rose sharply after torrential rain over Uttarakhand and western UP, pushing floodwater into riverbank settlements at Prayagraj and putting Ganga–Yamuna danger marks under watch.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Prayagraj (Sangam of Ganga & Yamuna) — Uttar Pradesh. At the confluence (Sangam) of the Ganga and the Yamuna in the southern Doab; upstream the Yamuna passes Delhi–Agra–Etawah, the Ganga passes Kanpur; downstream the combined river runs to Varanasi and the Ghaghara/Son junctions.

features.name: Pakal Dul / Marusudar
features.fact: the 1,000 MW Pakal Dul project (CVPPL/NHPC) — which will carry India's tallest dam on the Indus system (167 m) — is being pushed to commissioning through September–December 2026, part of the accelerated Chenab build-out after the Indus Waters Treaty was put in abeyance.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Pakal Dul dam & the Marusudar river — Kishtwar district, Jammu & Kashmir. On the Marusudar, the largest tributary of the Chenab, in the Chenab valley between the Pir Panjal and the Great Himalaya; Kishtwar lies east of Doda, with the Kiru, Kwar and Ratle projects on the same stretch.

features.name: Vizhinjam
features.fact: India's first deepwater transshipment port began full EXIM (export–import) operations from Aug 18, reviewed again in late August; Kerala simultaneously launched "Mission Samudra", a port-led plan for a Vizhinjam Maritime Economic Region along the state's 600-km coast — a direct challenge to Colombo, Singapore and Jebel Ali.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Vizhinjam (Thiruvananthapuram) — Kerala. On the Arabian Sea/Malabar coast about 16 km south of Thiruvananthapuram, next to Kovalam and close to Cape Comorin (Kanniyakumari); it sits ~10 nautical miles off the east–west international shipping lane, with a natural depth of ~20 m.

features.name: Bharat Mandapam / Delhi
features.fact: India, chairing BRICS in 2026 under the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," will host the 18th BRICS Summit here on Sep 12–13 — announcements and sherpa-level preparation ran through the first week of September.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan — New Delhi. On the Yamuna's right bank in the National Capital Territory, the venue that hosted the 2023 G20 summit.

features.name: Kargil–Leh corridor (Kargil anchor)
features.fact: a fortnight-long "Ladakh Peace and Justice March" from Kargil to Leh was announced in late August for Sep 10–24, timed to the first anniversary of the 2025 Leh firing, reviving the demand for statehood and Sixth Schedule status for Ladakh.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kargil → Leh, Ladakh (UT). Kargil sits on the Suru river (an Indus tributary) in the trans-Himalayan Zanskar range, linked to the Kashmir valley by the Zoji La pass; Leh lies downstream on the Indus itself, below the Ladakh range and the Khardung La.

features.name: Zhangpu / Taiwan Strait coast
features.fact: Typhoon Saudel, the 18th storm of the 2026 Pacific season, made a rare third landfall at Zhangpu on Sep 3 after two landfalls at Yuhuan on Aug 28; 83,000+ were evacuated in Fujian and more than 100 houses collapsed at Huating, Putian.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Zhangpu (Zhangzhou), Fujian — with Yuhuan, Zhejiang, China. Zhangpu is on Fujian's south coast facing the Taiwan Strait, near Xiamen; Putian lies up the same coast; Yuhuan is an island-county of Taizhou, Zhejiang, on the East China Sea.

features.name: Johnson Bayou
features.fact: Tropical Storm Edouard came ashore here on Sep 1 with 60 mph winds, then stalled over east Texas and dumped 10–21 inches of rain, knocking out power to 150,000+ customers.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Johnson Bayou (Cameron Parish), Louisiana — USA. On the Gulf of Mexico coast right at the Texas–Louisiana line, beside Sabine Pass and Sabine Lake, west of the Atchafalaya basin and east of Galveston Bay.

features.name: Anak Krakatau
features.fact: a major eruption at 00:50 WIB on Sep 5 threw ash to about 15 km (50,000 ft), tracked west by the Darwin VAAC — a live aviation and tsunami-risk concern on one of the world's busiest sea lanes.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Anak Krakatau & the Sunda Strait — Indonesia. The "child of Krakatoa" cone in the Sunda Strait, the channel separating Sumatra from Java and linking the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean; the 1883 caldera collapse and the 1927 rebirth of the cone happened here.

features.name: Mount Sinabung
features.fact: Indonesia's Geological Agency raised Sinabung to Level III (Siaga) after an Aug 31 eruption sent ash ~3,500 m above the summit — its first serious reactivation in several years.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Mount Sinabung — Karo, North Sumatra, Indonesia. A stratovolcano in the Barisan range of northern Sumatra, close to Lake Toba (the world's largest volcanic lake) and the Toba caldera, inland of Medan.

features.name: Natanz region
features.fact: on Sep 5 the US president said Washington might "hit" the site "very soon" — the deeply buried (100 m+) hall that the IAEA has never been allowed to inspect — as US–Iran strikes continued through early September.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La ("Pickaxe Mountain") & Natanz — Isfahan province, Iran. On Iran's arid Central Plateau, ~225 km south of Tehran, immediately south of the Natanz enrichment complex and north of Isfahan, in the shadow of the Zagros.

features.name: Niamey / Niger
features.fact: on the night of Aug 28–29 mutinous junior officers — reportedly drawn from the jihadist-hit Dosso, Téra and Tillabéri regions — seized the airport, state radio and TV in a coup attempt; the Presidential Guard, with Russian backing, retook Base 101, and the junta declared the plot foiled.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Niamey & Base 101 — Niger (with the Tillabéri, Téra and Dosso regions). Niamey stands on the Niger river in south-western Niger; Base 101 adjoins Diori Hamani airport. Tillabéri covers the Liptako-Gourma tri-border with Mali and Burkina Faso (Téra and Ouallam within it); Dosso lies south toward the Benin/Nigeria frontier.

features.name: Kyiv / Dnieper corridor
features.fact: Sep 1–2 brought a sixth consecutive night of mass Russian missile-and-drone strikes, killing at least a dozen in Kyiv (seven of them at a railway depot) and hitting Odesa and Dnipro as the school year opened.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kyiv, Odesa and Dnipro — Ukraine. Kyiv on the Dnieper (Dnipro) in the north; Dnipro city downstream in the industrial east; Odesa the Black Sea port near the Dniester estuary and the Danube delta.
